questions.explanation: Real rate equals nominal minus expected inflation, so 8% minus 3% equals 5%; adding would overstate it.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute the structural deficit from actual and cyclical values
questions.stem: Chef53's recipe costing sheet lists actual deficit 17 and cyclical deficit 7; what structural deficit results?
questions.explanation: Structural deficit equals actual minus cyclical, so 17 minus 7 equals 10; adding would double count the cycle.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Combine debt and deficit stages into a conclusion
questions.stem: Chef54's recipe costing sheet shows debt 100, deficit 20, GDP 200; which two-stage conclusion is correct?

options.text: Stage one adds cyclical and stage two overstates structural deficit.
Stage one gives new debt 120 and stage two gives a 60% debt-to-GDP ratio.
Stage one skips the adjustment and stage two repeats the raw figure.
Stage one reverses the inputs and stage two inverts the conclusion.

questions.explanation: New debt is 120 against GDP of 200, giving 60%; ignoring the deficit understates the ratio.
questions.hint: Add deficit, then divide by GDP.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: State how spending and revenue define the deficit
questions.stem: Chef55's recipe costing sheet shows spending 70 and revenue 45; what does the deficit measure?

options.text: A deficit is the same as total government debt.
A deficit occurs only when revenue exceeds spending.
A deficit equals spending minus revenue in that period.
A deficit is measured as revenue minus spending.

questions.explanation: A deficit is a flow of spending over revenue in one period, not the accumulated debt stock.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the structural deficit after cyclical adjustment
questions.stem: Chef56's recipe costing sheet adjusts a 9 deficit with a 2 cyclical component; which structural deficit is correct?

options.text: Structural deficit equals 9 plus 2, or 11.
Structural deficit equals the cyclical 2 alone.
Structural deficit equals the actual 9 with no adjustment.
Structural deficit equals 9 minus 2, or 7.

questions.explanation: Removing the 2 cyclical component from the 9 actual deficit leaves 7 structural; adding or ignoring misstates it.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain the real rate from nominal and inflation
questions.stem: Chef57's recipe costing sheet records nominal rate 5% and inflation 2%; explain the real rate.

answer.exemplar: The real rate is 3% because 5% nominal minus 2% inflation preserves purchasing power; using nominal alone would overstate the true cost of borrowing.

questions.explanation: Subtracting inflation from nominal gives the real rate; ignoring inflation overstates the true cost of borrowing.
